The [case study](../../cases/eu-frames/index.qmd), which presents the original paper, the Multi100 project and the five reanalyses on which every track of the case is built, is the place to start.

This version of the one-day course on the EU-frames case keeps the practices of open research in the foreground. Across the day you work as analyst no. 6 on a claim of the original author (OA) of a paper about how citizens of the member states frame the European Union, a claim that five analysts reanalysed for the Multi100 project. You meet the debate about the credibility of social science, the three Rs of reproduction, robustness and replication, and the places where the data, code and plans of a study are kept. You read the paper and write an estimand statement for its claim. You reproduce, to the third decimal, the result that Multi100 recorded for one of the three analysts whose analyses rest on means of countries or of cells, chosen by you, and you read the code that the analyst deposited for the slip that it carries. And you write a preregistration for a replication of that analysis on later waves of the survey, without running it. The day uses no menu of specifications and no class chart, and nothing is submitted.

The day works on aggregate data only, the country-year panel of the course and two files that the course rebuilt for two of the analysts, and it is taught in the [browser lab](../../cases/eu-frames/lab.qmd), which runs R inside a web page with the data in place, so nothing needs to be installed. The downloadable workspace is the option for those who have installed R and an IDE (Positron, RStudio, VS Code, etc.), and it gives the same numbers. The day runs as four parts of ninety minutes, with breaks of thirty, sixty and thirty minutes between them. Several of its steps are things that the class does together, such as everyone typing the analyst and the t-statistic that they have reproduced and holding it back until the facilitator says go, so the day needs a facilitator.

| | What happens | Length |
|---|---|---|
| [Before the day](before.qmd) | Open the browser lab once and read the case study; installing R and an IDE is optional. | about an hour |
| [Part 1 – Credibility and open research](part-1.qmd) | What a claim is for, why the field talks of a crisis, the three Rs and the SCORE programme, the five Multi100 analysts, and where data, code and plans are kept; then the browser lab runs on every machine. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 2 – The claim and its estimand](part-2.qmd) | The paper in full, estimands, and the five questions that the analysts answered; you write your estimand statement. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 3 – The reproduction](part-3.qmd) | You reproduce the recorded result of C6HJR, KQXUE or 018OL, then read the code that the analyst deposited and find its slip. | 90 minutes |
| [Part 4 – Replication and preregistration](part-4.qmd) | The claim on new data, what a preregistration fixes, and a preregistration for a replication, written and not run. | 90 minutes |
| [After the day](after.qmd) | Where to go next in the companion curriculum. | as you like |

The other two one-day formats on this case put the [data tools](../eu-frames-one-day-data-tools/index.qmd) or the [statistical methods](../eu-frames-one-day-methods/index.qmd) in the foreground, and the [three-day course](../eu-frames-three-days/index.qmd) builds the data from the raw survey files and reproduces all five analysts.
